A target is route:<id> (routes below), node:<id> (another piece of the manual) or doc:<repo path>#<anchor> (a GitHub doc, doc_base with the ref for the server's version). {admin}, {preview} and {plugin} are pills; {wake} is the wake word (wake_word below).

notes.live: Filled from the server when the page shows: things-to-say = GET /api/capabilities/manual (each handler's display.label, example_phrases, requires_network, origin; where it lists no phrases, the manual's own phrases for that handler; a handler in handler_needs_feature shows only while GET /api/capabilities features names that feature on); rooms = GET /api/satellites; plugins = GET /api/plugins; wake-word = the satellites' wake_word / wake_phrase. Nothing extra shows when it can't be read.
notes.checklist: done_when: admin_claimed (GET /api/auth/status setup_complete), internet_answered (GET /api/config internet_access not ''), rooms (GET /api/satellites not empty), room_heard (a room has a session: GET /api/satellites/<room>/sessions), people (GET /api/people not empty), music (GET /api/music/library/stats total_tracks > 0), phone_app (an android device in GET /api/devices, admin only), this_phone_paired (the app, paired). A read that fails leaves the line unticked, never ticked.
notes.doc_ref: More-detail links open the docs of the version the server runs: the tag v<label> when the version label is a release exactly (1.0.0, 1.0.0-rc2), else main. The label is GET /api/config/version's version.
notes.phrases: handler/path: what the router does with the phrase (fast = a fast path; llm = the tool model; qa = no handler). pending: being built elsewhere. domovoi/tests/test_manual_content.py routes the fast ones.

wake_word.note: Some rooms answer to another word: {list}.

blocks.text: **Domovoi is your home's own voice assistant.** It runs on a computer in your house, the Domovoi server. Small speakers with microphones put it in every room. Your voice never leaves your home network.
Three ways to use it

items.text: **Talk to a room.** Say {wake}, then what you want: "set a timer for 10 minutes." Your household can also train a word of its own: see [Wake word and greeting](node:wake-word).
**The dashboard.** Open it in any browser on your Wi-Fi, at the address whoever set up Domovoi gave you (it ends in `:6369`). You can manage music, files, chat, people and settings there.
**The Domovoi app** on Android phones. It has the everyday pages, a music player and chat, and it plays the phone's own music when there is no server.

blocks.text: Try saying

phrases.note: checks online, if you allow it

phrases.text: play some jazz in the kitchen

blocks.text: Getting set up
blocks.note: a checklist; each line ticks itself when it's done

checklist.text: **Claim the admin account** {admin}: [Settings → Advanced](route:settings/advanced), **set up admin**. Type the 8-word setup code and choose a password. Where the code is: the Windows installer shows it on its last page; on Linux it is in a file on the server. [More detail](doc:README.md#2-claim-the-admin-account)
**Answer the internet question**: Yes, Sometimes or No. You can change it later in [Settings → Internet](route:settings/internet).
**Add your first room**: [Settings → Rooms](route:settings/rooms). See [A Raspberry Pi room](node:pi-room).
**Say the wake word** in that room: {wake}, then "what time is it?"
**Introduce yourself** in that room: "my name is …", then "yes".
**Add your music**: [Music](route:music), **Upload**, or copy files into the server's music folder.
**Put the app on your phones**: [Settings → Phones & browsers → Get the Domovoi app](route:settings/phones-and-browsers).

topics.title: How it works
topics.subtitle: your home's own assistant
topics.intro: A room hears you and the server thinks. The answer plays in the room you're in. Everything runs on machines in your home.

pieces.title: Hears
pieces.subtitle: the wake word, then your words

blocks.text: The wake word is heard by the room itself: a Raspberry Pi, a spare computer, or a phone in room mode. Nothing is sent until it hears it. Then the room streams what you say to the server over your home network. There, **Whisper** turns it into text.

items.text: On a server set up by the installer (Linux script or Windows), Whisper runs on the processor, with its small English model.
A server set up by hand can run Whisper on an NVIDIA graphics card instead.

blocks.text: Most commands ("set a timer", "pause the music") are recognised instantly, with no AI model. When a command isn't, a **routing model** picks the right feature. Open questions go to an **answer model**, and pictures in chat go to a **vision model**. All of them run on the server, through Ollama.

header: Server with 24 GB of memory or more

blocks.text: Those are what the installers pick. A server set up by hand starts with Qwen2.5 14B for routing.
An NVIDIA graphics card makes them faster: Ollama uses it by itself, on Linux and on Windows. An admin can change models in [Settings → Models](route:settings/models).

**AI chat and questions are optional.** The installers ask whether to include them, and an admin can turn them off or on at any time under **AI chat and questions** in [Settings → Models](route:settings/models). Off, no routing, answer or vision model is used: voice commands still work on their usual phrases, and so do speech recognition, the voices and the wake word. A question then gets "I'm set up for home commands", and Chat is hidden. Turning them on shows the download size first, then downloads the models.

pieces.title: Speaks
pieces.subtitle: three voices, all on the server

blocks.text: Replies are spoken on the server, in one of three voices: **Kristin** (the default), **Norman** or **Linda**. Each room plays the reply through its own speaker. If a voice is missing, a plain system voice speaks instead, so Domovoi is never silent. See [Domovoi's voice](node:voice).
A database on the server keeps everything: settings, people, timers, conversations and play history. See [What's kept](node:kept) for how long each is kept.

pieces.title: Plays
pieces.subtitle: a music player for every room

blocks.text: Every room gets its own music player on the server. It streams to that room's speaker, so two rooms can play different things at once. Your music, videos, pictures and documents stay in ordinary folders on the server.

pieces.title: The server
pieces.subtitle: Linux, or a Windows PC; GPU optional

blocks.text: One computer that stays on. Either:

items.text: **Linux** (Ubuntu 26.04: one script installs everything), or
**a Windows 11 PC** with the Windows installer {preview}, which puts the same Linux server inside Windows, out of sight.

blocks.text: On a Windows PC:

items.text: With 16 GB of memory it gets the smaller models; with 32 GB, the standard ones and wake-word training.
Whisper always runs on the processor there.

blocks.text: A graphics card is optional everywhere.

items.text: The **dashboard** is the web page where you manage everything; it's the only place to install plugins and change server settings.
The **app** brings the everyday pages to your phone, plus its own player, chat mic and offline assistant.

blocks.text: Timers count down and ring. Reminders say your message out loud when the time comes: in a while ("in 20 minutes") or at a clock time ("at 6 pm", "tomorrow morning", "on Friday at 5"). Both are heard around the house. Domovoi says back the time it set. A time on its own means the next time it comes; add morning, evening, am or pm to be sure.
Try saying

phrases.text: set a timer for 8 minutes for the pasta
how much time is left on the timer
remind me to call Mom in 20 minutes
remind me in 2 hours to take the bins out
remind me at 6 pm to take the bins out

blocks.text: Also
Your timers show on [Home](route:home) and in each room's **Timers** tab ([Settings → Rooms](route:settings/rooms)).
If Home's timers card says "Timers may ring a few minutes late on this phone", tap **allow alarms**.
If something's wrong

items.text: A wake-up or an alarm is spoken in the room, like a reminder; it doesn't ring.
Times are the server's own time, the one "what time is it" answers in. If they're hours off, ask whoever set up Domovoi to set the server's time zone.

blocks.text: Domovoi knows the time, does maths and answers questions. For anything that changes (weather, scores, prices) it offers to check online, if your household allows the internet.
Try saying

phrases.text: split $120 4 ways with a 20 percent tip

blocks.text: If something's wrong

items.text: "I'm set to stay off the internet": your household chose No in [Settings → Internet](route:settings/internet).

"I'm set up for home commands" or "I can't look that up with AI turned off": AI chat and questions are off for your home. Commands still work; an admin can turn AI on in [Settings → Models](route:settings/models).
"My question-answering model isn't installed yet": AI is on but its model hasn't been downloaded. An admin can download it in [Settings → Models](route:settings/models).
"My search helper isn't running": ask whoever set up Domovoi.
An answer sounds wrong? Say "are you sure?".

blocks.text: Play your own music in the room you're in, or in any other room by naming it.
Try saying

phrases.text: play some music in the garage
in the garage, stop the music
phrases.note: say the room first to stop, pause or skip somewhere else

phrases.try: play the song that goes warm stones by the fire

phrases.text: when I say Gramps I mean Hearth Ensemble
phrases.note: a nickname for an artist in your library

blocks.text: If something's wrong
"no speakers set up" means no room has connected yet. "That room's speaker is offline": check [Your rooms](node:rooms). More in [Music and room queues](node:music).
An **announcement** is spoken in other rooms. A **drop-in** is a live two-way call into a room.
Try saying
On a room's page, tap **drop in from this phone** to talk to that room.
If something's wrong

Drop-ins need a room with an echo-cancelling microphone (the XVF3800 board, or most phones in room mode). A room may be set to ask before it answers: [Settings → Advanced](route:settings/advanced), **Drop-in** {admin}.
Notes are quick jottings, kept by the room and the time. Memory keeps facts about *you*, so it needs to know your voice first (see [People and voices](node:people)).
Try saying

phrases.text: jot down buy milk and eggs
remember that I parked on level 3
what do you remember about me
forget that I parked on level 3

blocks.text: Also
Notes show in each room's **Notes** tab ([Settings → Rooms](route:settings/rooms)). Memories show on [People](route:people), under each person's **Memory** tab.

This lists every feature this Domovoi has, including installed plugins, with phrases to try. It also says which features work offline, which work less well offline, and which need the internet. Install a plugin and its features appear here.
Ask "what can you do?" out loud and Domovoi names a few of these, with one thing to say for each; this page has them all.
Try saying
Try saying
Wait for the greeting or chime after the wake word, then speak. Words said over the greeting aren't heard.
If something's wrong

items.text: It doesn't wake: speak closer, or check the room is online in [Your rooms](node:rooms). An admin can make it more sensitive in the room's **Settings** tab.
It wakes on the TV: the same setting, the other way.
It misheard a name: introduce yourself again ("my name is …"), or fix how it *says* a word in [Domovoi's voice](node:voice).

blocks.text: Each room is one listening device: a Raspberry Pi, a spare laptop or a phone. [Settings → Rooms](route:settings/rooms) lists them. Each card shows:

items.text: online or offline;
what's playing;
its Wi-Fi signal;
when it last heard someone.

blocks.text: Open a room for its tabs. They are the icons along the top: **Overview** (the "i"), **Sessions**, **Conversations**, **Recently played**, **Notes**, **Timers**, **Logs**, and **Settings** (the gear).
How to

items.text: Make a room hear the wake word more or less easily, swap its greeting for a chime, or make its voice louder: its **Settings** tab, **Wake sensitivity**, **Wake acknowledgement**, **Voice loudness boost**.
A Pi or spare computer acting up: **Restart satellite**. Updating it: **Upgrade satellite**.
A room moved to new hardware: **Reset pairing**, then approve the new device.

blocks.text: [Settings → Rooms](route:settings/rooms) shows the same rooms.
Try saying
If something's wrong

items.text: *offline*: power and Wi-Fi first. If **every** room says *can't connect*, see [Restarting](node:restart).
The Wi-Fi bar is amber or red: move the room device or the router closer.
A room says "having trouble reaching the network": it has lost the server.

blocks.text: The usual room: a Raspberry Pi with a microphone board and a speaker. About the price of a smart speaker. [Parts list](doc:docs/SATELLITE_HARDWARE.md)
How to

items.text: Put Raspberry Pi OS Lite (64-bit) on a microSD card, and put the card in the server's card reader.

[Settings → Rooms](route:settings/rooms) → **prepare satellite media** → **wi-fi setup portal** → **Prepare**. On the Windows install, which can't see SD cards, **download overlay zip** and unzip it onto the card.
Start the Pi with the card. It makes its own Wi-Fi network, `Domovoi-Setup-<id>`. Join it from your phone, pick your home Wi-Fi and name the room.
The Pi says a six-digit code. Under **waiting for approval**, type it and press **approve**.

blocks.text: If something's wrong
**show setup details** on the card lists the setup network and its page.
A Linux or Windows 10/11 laptop or PC can be a room. Use one that stays plugged in, with sleep turned off. Not the computer that runs Domovoi.
How to

items.text: [Settings → Rooms](route:settings/rooms) → **add a spare device**. Type the room's name, press **make the code**.
**Linux:** press **copy the command** and run it on that computer, signed in as the account it should use.

**Windows:** on that PC, signed in as the account it should use, press **Download the Windows Setup** (or type the short address the card shows into its browser) and open the file. The setup code is in its name, so there is nothing to type. If the card shows only a command, paste that into PowerShell on the PC instead (a Linux server may offer **get the Windows Setup** first).
Windows says **"Windows protected your PC"**: click **More info**, then **Run anyway**. Domovoi isn't signed by Microsoft yet; the file comes from your own server.
The computer shows a six-digit code. Approve it under **waiting for approval**.

blocks.text: A tray icon shows when the microphone is live, and mutes it. The PowerShell command is still there for Windows, under **advanced**.
If something's wrong
A processor from before about 2009 is refused. A setup code lasts 24 hours: make a new one if Setup says it's unknown.

pieces.title: An old phone or tablet as a room
pieces.subtitle: room mode

blocks.text: An Android 8 or newer phone on its charger becomes a room ("room mode"): it hears the wake word, answers, plays the room's music, and takes announcements.
How to

items.text: {admin} once: [Settings → Rooms](route:settings/rooms) → **prepare satellite media** → **Refresh caches**. This gives phones the wake word.
{admin} **add a spare device**, name the room, **make the code**. A QR code appears.
Scan it with the phone's camera. The page installs the Domovoi app (press **Download the app to this server** there once first) and opens it as that room.
Read the explainer, press **Start room mode**, allow the microphone, press **Become this room**.
Approve the six-digit code on the dashboard.

blocks.text: A phone that already has the app can do this from [Settings → Rooms](route:settings/rooms) → **Use this device as a room**, or from the **Domovoi Room** icon.
To leave, hold **exit room mode**, unlock, then choose **Keep this room** or **Forget this room**.
If something's wrong

items.text: *mic blocked*: turn the microphone back on in quick settings.
After a restart: tap the notification to resume.
Turn off battery optimisation for Domovoi.

pieces.title: An old computer, from a USB stick
pieces.subtitle: the stick sets it up

blocks.text: The server makes a USB stick. An old 64-bit PC, laptop or 2012–2017 Intel Mac starts from it and becomes a room that does nothing else. **This erases that computer's disk.** It needs a network cable while it sets up.
How to

items.text: **add a spare device** → name the room → **make the code** → under **old computer (usb stick)**, **Prepare the stick**.
**Open in Raspberry Pi Imager** to write it to a USB stick (2 GB or more).
Start the old computer from the stick (its boot-menu key, often F12), type **ERASE** when asked, and wait about half an hour.
Approve the code it shows.

pieces.title: Wake word and greeting
pieces.subtitle: the word a room wakes to

blocks.text: A new room wakes to {wake}. After waking, it greets you or chimes, then listens.
Train your own wake word

items.text: Where: [Settings → Wake words](route:settings/wake-words). The admin turns training on once, with **Turn on wake-word training**.
What it needs: a server with 24 GB of memory, about 22 GB of downloads and about 32 GB of disk. A word takes about 20 minutes to train with an NVIDIA graphics card, and over an hour on the processor.
The steps: **Create** the word, **Record** 15 or more clips on a satellite in the room itself, press **Train**, then **Push to room**.
A wake word trained at home is for your household only ([why](doc:docs/LICENSES.md#the-wake-word-trainer)).

blocks.text: Greetings

items.text: What a room says when it wakes: [Settings → Greetings](route:settings/greetings).
A chime or a light instead: the room's **Settings** tab, **Wake acknowledgement**.

blocks.text: Three voices, all on the server: **Kristin** (default), **Norman** and **Linda**.
How to

items.text: Pick one: [Settings → Voices](route:settings/voices) → **Domovoi's voice** → play a sample, **use this voice** {admin}.
A word said wrong? **Say it like**: type the word and how it sounds, the stressed part in capitals (Siobhan = shiv-AWN). Press play to hear it first.
How *this phone* speaks: [Settings → Voices](route:app/voice): "Same as the server" or one of the three (about 64 MB, downloaded once).

blocks.text: Try saying
The Domovoi app runs on Android 8.0 or newer, older 32-bit phones included. It comes from your own server; no store is needed.
How to

items.text: On the dashboard, [Settings → Phones & browsers → Get the Domovoi app](route:settings/phones-and-browsers) shows a QR code. If it says the app isn't on the server yet, ask whoever set up Domovoi to press **Download the app to this server**.
Scan the code with the phone's camera and install. Android asks you to allow installs from your browser once.
Open Domovoi. Tap **connect** at the top, pick your server (it scans your Wi-Fi), and press **trust this server**. Can't see it? Use **add manually** with the dashboard's address.
**pair this phone**: type the household token. An admin finds it in [Settings → Phones & browsers → Household token](route:settings/phones-and-browsers).

blocks.text: Switch or forget a server from the server name at the top, or in [Settings → Phones & browsers](route:app/connection).
If something's wrong
"App not installed" means a 32-bit phone; take the 32-bit app from the same page.

pieces.title: Music on the phone
pieces.subtitle: here or in a room, saved offline

blocks.text: **Play here** plays on the phone; **play in room** plays in a room.
How to

items.text: Save a song, episode or video to the phone with **save to device** (or **save**). Files go to Downloads/Domovoi and play with no server.

Save a book with **save to phone** on its page. The size shows first. Books stay inside the app, play with their chapters with no server, and keep one place in step with the server. A save that stops when you leave home finishes by itself when the server is in reach again.
Music, Videos, Audiobooks and Files switch between the server and **your device**. From your device you can upload to the server. In Files, **add folder** shows a folder of the phone's own.

pieces.title: Chat and the chat mic
pieces.subtitle: type, talk, send photos and documents

blocks.text: **Chat** holds your chats with Domovoi: those **on home server** (see [Chat](node:chat)), shared with the household, and those **on this phone** (the assistant, below). Each chat shows where it runs, and a new one starts where you chatted last.

Chat opens on your chats, pinned ones first, then the most recent; type in **Message Domovoi…** at the bottom to start a new one. A chat is named by its first words, then Domovoi gives it a short title after the first reply; a name you give it stays.
How to

items.text: Long-press a chat (or its **chat actions** button) to **rename**, **pin** (pins stay on this phone), **archive**, **share** or **delete** it; swipe to archive. Archived chats are under **archived** at the end of the list.
**search chats** finds words in titles and messages, in both kinds of chat.
Long-press a reply to **copy**, **share** or **try again**.
A line saying **earlier messages are beyond what Domovoi can keep in mind** marks where the model stops seeing the older part of a long chat.
Tap **talk** to speak a message: **hold to talk**, release to send, slide away to cancel. Up to 30 seconds.
"my name is …" in the chat mic teaches Domovoi your voice from this phone.
**attach image**: up to 4 pictures. Phone photos in HEIC are turned into a JPEG on the phone first (Android 9 or newer), without their location.

**attach a document**: a PDF, Word, OpenDocument, Excel, CSV, text or markdown file, then ask about it. In a chat **on this phone** it is read on the phone and stays there. The answer lists the pages it came from; tap one to see the passage (a PDF shows the page itself).
A PDF needs Android 15 (or 12 to 14 with the PDF update) to be read on the phone. Otherwise **ask the home server** reads its text and sends it back; nothing is kept there.
In [Files](route:files), the question mark on a document starts a chat about it: a file on this phone in a phone chat, a file in the home server's Documents in a home-server chat.

**Summarize a long document:** it is read in parts, with "reading part 3 of 8 · about 1 min left" and **stop**. Stop keeps what was read; **carry on** reads the rest. Leave Chat and it pauses at the end of the part, then carries on when you come back.

**use home server** appears only when your home server is measured to be faster than this phone for that document (reading all of it, plus sending it). It sends the file to be read there; nothing is kept there. If the server can't finish, Chat says so and offers **read it on this phone**.

blocks.text: A Domovoi that runs on the phone itself: type or talk, in airplane mode too. It knows the time and date, and it answers questions. It also knows the phone: what's playing, the battery, free space, Wi-Fi or mobile data, your next alarm, Do Not Disturb, which phone and Android this is, and which songs, videos and saved books are on it. It can't set timers, play music or look things up online. House things (rooms, house timers, the household calendar) are in your home server chats.

"Text Sam", "call Mom", "email Alex", "directions to the station", "add lunch tomorrow at noon to my calendar", "open a link" and "share this" show a card first; a tap opens the app that does it, and you finish there. Your calendar, where you are and calling people by name each ask for permission the first time, with the reason; say no and it simply says it can't, and never asks again. Everything is read on the phone and never sent anywhere; a phone chat never asks your home server.
How to
**Chat** → **new chat** → **on this phone** → **Set up the assistant on this phone** → **download** (the button shows the size, about 2.6 GB). It waits for Wi-Fi unless you **allow mobile data**.

It needs a 64-bit phone with 8 GB of memory or more. To report a bad reply, long-press it. **Export all phone chats** (in a phone chat, the model settings button) saves them as Markdown and JSON where you pick. Its chats stay on the phone, marked **on this phone**; away from home they are the only ones Chat lists. They never mix with your home server's chats.
See [An old phone or tablet as a room](node:phone-room). A phone you also use every day needs a screen lock. While it is a room, the rest of the app is locked.

items.text: [Settings → App layout](route:settings/app-layout): pick 2 to 5 tabs for the bottom of the screen. Home always comes first.
[Settings → Voices](route:app/voice): how this phone speaks.
The app's Settings has the dashboard's groups and names. What only the dashboard can change (greetings, wake words, models, Advanced, …) says so there, with **Open on the dashboard**.

**Updates:** when your server has a newer app, Home shows "Domovoi … is available from your server". Tap **get the update**. [Settings → About & updates](route:settings/about) → **App updates** says which version you have. A Google Play install updates itself.
[Settings → About & updates](route:settings/about) → **Privacy** says what the app keeps.

blocks.text: Your music library, on the server, played in any room or in the browser.
How to

items.text: Add music: [Music](route:music) → **Upload**, or copy files into the server's music folder.
Each room has one shared queue, and anyone in the house can add to it.
[Music → Room queue](route:music/queue): drag to reorder. A room card's **queue** button goes straight there.
[Music](route:music/queue) → **room queue**: **play next**, **move up** and **move down** on each song.
Playlists and favorites: [Music → Playlists](route:music/playlists).
Each queued song says which device added it.

blocks.text: Try saying

phrases.text: how many songs do I have
what did I add this week

blocks.text: Also
Guests on your Wi-Fi can change the queue of a room that's playing. See [Guests, household, admin](node:guests).

pieces.title: Lyrics
pieces.subtitle: see the words, find a song

blocks.text: The **lyrics** button in the player shows a song's words, timed when it has them. Words come from the song file, or, if your household allows the internet, from LRCLIB.
Try saying

phrases.try: play the song that goes warm stones by the fire

blocks.text: How to
[Podcasts](route:podcasts) → **subscribe**: search by name, or paste a feed (**by RSS URL**). New episodes download by themselves only if your internet answer is Yes.
Try saying

phrases.text: play the latest episode of The Daily
resume the podcast in the kitchen

blocks.text: Books in the server's audiobooks folder, with chapters, resumed where you left off.
How to
[Audiobooks](route:audiobooks) → **play**; **reindex** after adding books. In the app, open a book for its chapters and **save to phone**; **add** sends books from the phone to the server.
Try saying

phrases.text: play my audiobook in the office

blocks.text: Every video in your libraries, played in the browser or the app, resuming where you stopped. [Videos](route:videos)
A spoken briefing from the feeds your household picks, plus each person's own topics.
How to
[News](route:news) → **add topic**, or add a feed.
Try saying

phrases.text: any news about the city council

blocks.text: Shown when the radio plugin is installed. Find stations on the **Stations** page and star the ones you like. Domovoi plays favorites by name.
Try saying

pieces.title: Chat
pieces.subtitle: type to Domovoi, pictures and documents too

blocks.text: Type to Domovoi. Answers come from the models on your server.
How to

[Chat](route:chat) → **new chat**. Press the paperclip to add up to 4 pictures (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP or BMP, 20 MB each). Beside each chat in the list: rename, archive and delete; **search chats** above the list, and **archived** at its end.

**Ask about a document:** the paperclip also takes a PDF, Word (.docx), OpenDocument (.odt), Excel (.xlsx), CSV, text or markdown file, up to 100 MB. Ask what it says. The answer names the pages or sections it came from; press one to see the passage, or to open a PDF at that page. If the document doesn't say, Domovoi answers "I couldn't find that in the document" instead of guessing. In [Files](route:files) → Documents, **Ask** on a file starts a chat about it.

**Look things up:** say "look up …", "what does this page say: https://…", or ask something Domovoi doesn't know. It searches its own manual and your offline library first, without asking. Before anything goes online it shows a card with the exact words and where they go: **Allow once**, **Allow in this chat** or **Not now**. The chip at the top of a chat says whether it may go online; chats that did show a globe. The answer lists what it read (Wikipedia's with "CC BY-SA 4.0"), and says "I couldn't find that" when what it read doesn't say. [Settings → Search](route:settings/search) {admin} has **Always allow internet** (off to start), the order of the sources, and **Use your own search** (your own SearXNG, or a Brave Search key).

**Summarize a long document:** ask for a summary and Domovoi reads it in parts, then combines them. The reply's place shows "reading part 3 of 8 · about 1 min left" (the time comes from how fast your server has been) with **stop**. Stop keeps what was read ("Summary of pages 1-9 (stopped)"), and **carry on** reads the rest. You can leave the page: the summary is there when you come back. A question asked by voice while it reads goes next, after the part being read (a few seconds on a GPU, up to about a minute on a server without one). Each point cites a page; a part Domovoi couldn't cite anything from is named under the summary. After a server restart the chat asks "carry on?" before it reads any more. One summary reads at a time per chat, and two in the house.
The picture button is **attach image**, and the app also takes HEIC photos. See [Chat and the chat mic](node:phone-chat).
If something's wrong

items.text: "Pictures need the vision model": ask whoever set up Domovoi to install it in [Settings → Models](route:settings/models).
Chat isn't there, or says "chat is off": AI chat and questions are off for your home. An admin can turn them on in [Settings → Models](route:settings/models).
A HEIC phone photo is refused on the dashboard: send it from the app, which converts it.
An old .doc or .rtf file: save it as .docx or PDF, then attach it again.
"pictures of text (scanned)": scanned pages aren't searched yet.
"set to stay off the internet": your home's internet answer is No ([Settings → Internet](route:settings/internet)); only the manual and the offline library are searched.
"Brave Search refused your key": check the key in [Settings → Search](route:settings/search); the answer came from Wikipedia meanwhile.
"Points that span parts may be missed": a long summary is made part by part. Ask about the specific thing to have it found wherever it is.

blocks.text: How to
[Files](route:files) → Documents → **New** → **Document**, **Spreadsheet**, **Drawing** or **Text file**. Each opens in its editor; press **Save**.
Opens text files and sheets from Files.
The household's events. [Calendar](route:calendar) → **new event**; switch between **month**, **week** and **day**.

pieces.title: Printers and scanners
pieces.subtitle: print and scan, by voice too

blocks.text: Domovoi prints to and scans from **network printers**: ones on your Wi-Fi or plugged into your router that work with **AirPrint**, **IPP Everywhere** or **Mopria**. That's almost every network printer from the last ten years; if your phone can print to it with no app, Domovoi can too. USB printers, and older printers that need a driver from the maker, don't work. Scanning needs a printer whose scanner works over AirPrint too (often called AirScan or eSCL).
How to

items.text: [Settings → Printers & scanners](route:settings/printers) shows the printers Domovoi can see. Press **Add** on yours, name it, then **Test page**. Not listed? Press **Look again**, or type its address under **Add by address** (on the printer's own screen or settings page).
One printer is the house's **Default**. A room can have its own default (**Default in rooms**): voice from that room prints there.
**Two-sided** and **Colour** follow the printer's own settings unless you switch them per printer.

**Print** sits on files in [Files](route:files) and Documents when a printer is set up: PDFs, pictures, text and markdown files, and spreadsheets (printed as a plain table). You pick the pages, copies, two-sided, colour and paper, and see a preview first.
Word and OpenDocument files don't print here: save them as PDF in Word or Docs first, then print the PDF.
**Scan** sits at the top of Documents when a scanner is set up. Scans are saved as one PDF in **Documents → Scans**, named by date.
Removing or renaming a printer needs the admin password {admin}.

blocks.text: Try saying

phrases.note: it tells you the pages and asks first

phrases.text: is the printer out of paper

blocks.text: If something's wrong

items.text: **Out of paper, jammed, cover open:** the printer's row says so in plain words, and a voice print that fails is said once in the room that asked. Fix it at the printer; the job carries on.
**"Level not reported":** some printers don't share their ink or toner levels. Check the printer's own screen.
**"Isn't answering":** the printer is off or asleep, or moved to a different network. Press **Look again**.
**"Security certificate changed":** usually a printer update or reset. An admin checks it and presses **Trust the new certificate**.
Each job is limited to 100 pages and 20 copies, and the house to 500 sheets a day; an admin can change the limits. The list of recent jobs is kept 90 days, and an admin can clear it.

blocks.text: Domovoi learns who's speaking, so memories, news topics and "who am I" are personal.
Try saying

phrases.note: deletes your voice, your memories and what you said; it must be your own voice

blocks.text: How to

items.text: Teach a new room your voice: say "my name is …" there. It asks "Is that you?"; say yes.
[People](route:people) shows everyone, when they were last heard, and their memories.
{admin} **rename**, **forget person**, or delete one wrong voice sample.

blocks.text: If something's wrong
Two people with the same name: an admin renames one on [People](route:people).

items.text: **Guests**: a phone or browser on your Wi-Fi that isn't paired. Guests can look around, and can change the music of a room that's playing.
**Household**: a paired phone or browser holds the household token. It can do everything day to day.
**Admin**: whoever has the admin password. Changes settings, installs plugins, approves rooms, deletes files.

blocks.text: How to

items.text: Sign in: [Settings → Advanced](route:settings/advanced) → **sign in**. A reload in that browser keeps you signed in for 60 minutes after you signed in; **sign out** ends it at once. Change the minutes in [Settings → Advanced](route:settings/advanced) → **Security** → **Stay signed in after a reload**.
Turn guest music control off: same place, **Guests can change the music in a playing room**.
The app never signs in as admin; it opens the dashboard for that.

blocks.text: If something's wrong
Forgot the admin password? It can only be reset on the server itself. Ask whoever set up Domovoi.
[Settings → Phones & browsers](route:settings/phones-and-browsers):

items.text: **This device**: give this browser or phone a name. It's what queues show as "added by".
**Queue access**, **Files access** {admin}: stop one device changing a room's music or the files.
**Guests** {admin}: ban a guest who keeps changing the music.
**mark as a shared screen** {admin}: for a kitchen tablet. Personal pages (People, Chat, Files, News) are left off it.

blocks.text: These settle household arguments; they aren't locks.
Everything stays on your server.

rows: What you said to Domovoi by voice, and its replies
90 days, or what **Keep voice history** says
Timers and reminders that went off
Command recordings (off unless an admin turns them on for a room)

blocks.text: Paired phones and browsers in the house can read the voice history, in each room's **Conversations** tab.
How to

items.text: "forget me", in your own voice: deletes your profile, voice samples, memories and everything you said to Domovoi.

{admin} [People](route:people) → **Voice history** → **Keep voice history**: 30 days, 90 days (the default), 1 year or Forever. Older turns are deleted every day. It's also in [Settings → Advanced](route:settings/advanced) → **Privacy**.
{admin} **Delete all voice history**, on the same page, deletes it all at once. People, voice samples, memories, notes, timers and chats stay.
{admin} **forget person** on [People](route:people) does what "forget me" does, for anyone: it deletes only what that person said.
"never save my voice": Domovoi stops learning it.
Delete a chat: the bin icon in [Chat](route:chat).
{admin} turn recordings off in a room's **Overview** (**Stop and delete**); the commands kept so far are in [Settings → Voice history](route:settings/voice-history).

{admin} listen to a room's command recordings, mark whether each one ended at the right moment, and delete them: [Settings → Voice history](route:settings/voice-history). A room keeps them only while an admin has turned them on for it.

blocks.text: An admin can change play history, news and timer history in [Settings → Advanced](route:settings/advanced).
Your voice never leaves the house, whatever you answer. The answer only decides the online extras.

items.text: **Yes, always**: web answers, lyrics lookups, artists' other names, podcast downloads.
**Sometimes**: the same, without automatic podcast downloads.
**No, keep everything in the house**: nothing goes out. Online buttons show "needs internet".

blocks.text: How to
[Settings → Internet](route:settings/internet) {admin}. Download what you need before choosing No.
[Settings → About & updates](route:settings/about) shows the release you run.
How to

items.text: **Check for updates**.
**Pull the latest**.
**Restart to apply changes**.

blocks.text: A failed update rolls itself back. **updates** chooses the channel: **stable** (releases only) or **main** (every change, as it lands). After an update, reload any open dashboard once.
See [App settings and updates](node:app-settings).
Some settings apply only after a restart: [Settings → About & updates](route:settings/about) → **Restart Domovoi** {admin}.

**If every room is offline but the dashboard opens**, the server's core has stopped answering. It restarts itself within about a minute. If it doesn't, an admin presses **Restart the core** (on [Home](route:home), [Settings → Rooms](route:settings/rooms) or [Settings → Health](route:settings/health)). The app says the core isn't answering, and reconnects by itself.
Try saying

phrases.note: how the server is: its processor, memory and disk

blocks.text: There's no backup button yet. What to keep safe:

items.text: the database;
the server's Domovoi folder: its identity, voices and trained wake words;
your media folders.

blocks.text: Keep the identity and the rooms won't need setting up again. A server set up by the installers also saves the database before every update.
The Windows installer can't keep your data through an uninstall yet. Ask whoever set up Domovoi.
Plugins add features: voice commands, pages, app screens.
How to

: [Plugins](route:plugins) → **Install from zip**, or **install from GitHub** → **fetch & preview**. Read the trust screen. **A plugin runs with full access to your server**, so install only from publishers you trust.
[Settings → Models](route:settings/models) shows the models in use:

items.text: **Speech-to-text**: hears you.
**Tool routing**: picks the feature.
**Q&A**: answers questions.
**Vision**: reads pictures in chat.

blocks.text: {admin} **Install** or **Switch** one. With an NVIDIA card, Qwen2.5-VL 7B reads pictures faster.

{admin} **AI chat and questions** at the top turns the AI models off or on for the whole home. Off keeps speech-to-text and hides the rest of the model rows. On says how much it will download (about 6.4 GB, or 9.1 GB on a server with 24 GB of memory or more) before it starts.

pieces.title: Asking Domovoi for help
pieces.subtitle: ask it, show it, report it

blocks.text: Domovoi answers questions about itself: from this manual, its FAQ and troubleshooting guide, and the help of the plugins you installed. It answers only from what it finds. When nothing covers the question, it says "The manual doesn't cover that." rather than guessing.
How to

items.text: Press **?** at the top of any page. Search the help, or press **ask Domovoi** to start a chat called "Help: …".
An error message has **ask Domovoi about this**: the help opens with the error's code and the page you were on.

In a chat, ask "how do I …?" or "why is the kitchen offline?". Domovoi also reads what its own checks show: rooms that are offline and why, plugins, its containers, and the last update (its details only for an admin).
**Something on your screen?** Paste or attach a screenshot in a chat on the home server. The vision model reads it on your server; it never leaves your home.
A chat on this phone answers from the app's own copy of the manual, offline. It can't read screenshots yet: use a home-server chat for those.

blocks.text: Try saying

phrases.text: how do I add a room
how do I change the wake word

blocks.text: After the short answer, Domovoi asks "Want me to send the steps to your phone?" Say yes, and they arrive as a chat called "Help: …" on the phones marked as yours ([Settings → Phones & browsers](route:app/connection), **This phone belongs to**, in the app). If Domovoi doesn't know your voice, it asks who to send them to. It never sends them to every phone.
If something's wrong

items.text: **AI chat and questions are off**: help still searches the manual and the docs, with no model, and screenshots can't be read. See [Models](node:models).

**Help can't solve it**: **report a problem**, in the **?** panel, builds a summary of your Domovoi with no passwords, codes, addresses or names. Read it, then copy or save it and post it yourself, on GitHub Discussions or Discord. Nothing is sent for you.
**A room doesn't answer**: see [Your rooms](node:rooms).
**Every room is offline**: see [Restarting](node:restart).
**"Just a moment, I'm waking up my language model"**: normal once after a restart.
**The dashboard looks old after an update**: reload the page once.
**A word is said wrong**: [Say it like](node:voice).
**Chat says pictures need the vision model**: [Models](node:models).
**Something is greyed with "needs internet"**: [Internet](node:internet).
**Not sure where to look**: ask Domovoi: [Asking Domovoi for help](node:help-desk).
**App: can't find the server**: same Wi-Fi as the server? **add manually** with the dashboard's address.
